a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is an eprosartan-like dianionic ARB with two carboxylic acids and a basic imidazole, fully ionized at physiological pH (neutral fraction 0, logD 0.56). The closest L4 permeability evidence, Exp3174, shows very low absorptive Caco-2 Papp (2.50 x 10^-8 cm/s) and high basolateral-to-apical Papp (25.6 x 10^-8 cm/s, ER ~10), with efflux persisting under BCRP/P-gp inhibition; this coherently supports absorption-limited F < 20%.

L6 hepatic-clearance/metabolic-stability records are for other molecules (azosemide, losartan, telmisartan, tienilic acid, suprofen, and cathinone analogs) and provide no query-specific hepatic extraction or metabolic-stability measurement. Suprofen is a CYP2C9 substrate yet has 92.2% absolute oral bioavailability, so CYP2C9 substrate status alone is not affirmative low-F evidence.
No L6 record overturns the L4 low-permeability/efflux evidence or provides a direct F measurement for the query; the low prediction is retained.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query.
No query-specific hepatic clearance, metabolic stability, or CYP reaction phenotyping data are available; L6 records are for other molecules.
No query-specific Caco-2/MDCK permeability, solubility, dissolution, or gut-wall efflux data are available; L4/L5 records are analogs.
No human PK, formulation, or dose data for the query are available; absorption may be formulation-dependent.
L1 high-F contexts are structurally distant from this dianionic ARB.
content.decision_summary: Kept low: the query is a fully ionized eprosartan-like dianionic ARB; L4 Exp3174 records show very low absorptive permeability and high efflux, and L6 hepatic-clearance/metabolic-stability records are not query-specific and do not change that assessment. No direct F measurement exists, but the coherent low-permeability/efflux evidence supports F < 20% better than F >= 20%.
